case_title: State of Gujarat & Anr. v. Narayan @ Narayan Sai @ Mota Bhagwan
accused_socioeconomic_status: Not stated by the Court. Alleged by the DGP that the accused has a financial background and a network of persons; no finding made.
previous_criminal_record: Not stated. No prior conviction mentioned; seven other offences were registered against the accused per the DGP, as allegations only.
aggravating_circumstances: As noted in the DGP order and accepted by the Court: threats to complainant and witnesses; attempts to threaten and suborn investigators; mass following; attempted bribery of officials; illegal mobile phone use in jail.
mitigating_circumstances: Argued by the accused: no violation during the December 2020 furlough; no complaints since 2016; mother's ill-health.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted; life imprisonment with fine of Rs. 1,00,000 for s.376(2) and s.377; shorter terms with fines for ss.354, 504, 506(2), 508, 323; compensation of Rs. 5,00,000 under s.357(3) CrPC; sentences concurrent.
high_court_outcome: Petition under s.482 CrPC allowed on 24 June 2021; DGP order of 8 May 2021 set aside; 14 days' furlough with police escort granted.
offence_finally_established: Convictions under ss.376(2), 377, 354, 504, 506(2), 508 and 323 IPC as recorded in the trial judgment; not disturbed in this appeal.
neutral_facts: An FIR was registered on 6 October 2013 at a police station alleging offences under the Indian Penal Code, including sexual offences against the victim, along with offences of intimidation, wrongful confinement and criminal conspiracy. Charges were framed after investigation. During the investigation, a police team was directed to arrest the accused, and the investigating officer's official phone details were publicised in the media to obtain information on the accused's whereabouts. Calls were later received threatening to kill the investigating officer, and the caller was booked. Police reported that a handwritten chit allegedly written by the accused was given to an administrator of a centre associated with the accused, seeking a bribe of one crore rupees, and that officials were allegedly bribed to weaken the case. Several witnesses were assaulted in 2014, with complaints registered against persons said to be followers of the accused. One witness was reportedly shot and later died during treatment. Police also reported that an inspector was threatened during the investigation, and that the accused allegedly kept a mobile phone in jail and attempted to contact outsiders. These matters are recorded as police allegations.
physical_harm: Not stated for the offences of conviction. Judgment notes alleged assaults on witnesses in 2014, one of which was fatal, attributed to followers of the accused and not part of the convicted offences.
number_of_offences: 13 charged; 7 finally upheld (ss.376(2), 377, 354, 504, 506(2), 508, 323 as recorded in the trial judgment; not disturbed by the Supreme Court)
key_evidence_accepted: No trial evidence was assessed. The Court accepted the DGP's grounds on public peace (jail mobile phone misuse, threats to witnesses, mass following, bribery attempts) as not perverse.
post_offence_conduct: Court noted the accused surrendered after the December 2020 furlough and interim bail; the Court also noted conduct in jail after trial was not shown to be above reproach.
custody_duration: About seven and a half years' imprisonment, as recorded by the High Court.
bail_history: Temporary bail for three weeks from 16 April 2015 and two days on 15 February 2019; furlough of 14 days from 5 December 2020; temporary bail from 31 January to 3 February 2021.
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR registered 6 October 2013); trial judgment: 30 April 2019; High Court: 24 June 2021; Supreme Court: 20 October 2021
legal_representation: For the State (appellants): Tushar Mehta, SG; Kanu Agrawal; Aniruddha P. Mayee. For the accused (respondent): Sanjiv Punalekar, Suvidutt M. S., Ankush Mahajan, Dharma Raj, Mrs. Anu B., Ms. Vijayalakshmi Raju, Mrs. Dhanya C.
investigation_status: FIR registered 6 October 2013; charges framed; trial concluded with conviction by the Sessions Court on 30 April 2019.
procedural_irregularity: None noted as a lapse by a lower court. The Court observed that the High Court's 2 December 2020 furlough order did not deal with the authorities' objections.
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted on 30 April 2019. High Court: Single Judge allowed the s.482 CrPC petition on 24 June 2021 and directed furlough. Supreme Court: State's appeal allowed; High Court order set aside.
prosecution_argument: Furlough is discretionary and subject to Rule 4; Rules 4(4), 4(6) and 4(10) bar release on public peace, conduct and escape grounds; the DGP's objections are valid and not addressed by the earlier High Court order; the gravity of the crimes and witness threats disentitle the accused.
defence_argument: Father is critically ill with multiple ailments and the only son is needed for care; the accused was released on furlough or temporary bail four times without incident; furlough is a right; Rule 3(2) allows release every year after seven years; no link to other attacks.
legal_principle_applied: Rules 3, 4 and 17 confer no legal right to furlough; furlough is discretionary, must be balanced against public interest, and may be refused under r.4(4) on public peace grounds; the Sanctioning Authority's opinion is reviewed only for perversity or extraneous considerations.
precedent_relied_upon: State of Maharashtra v. Suresh Pandurang Darvakar (2006) 4 SCC 776; Asfaq v. State of Rajasthan (2017) 15 SCC 55; State of Haryana v. Mohinder Singh (2000) 3 SCC 394
judicial_mitigating_factors: Court acknowledged the earlier release was for a genuine need (mother's health); no other mitigating factors weighed.
judicial_aggravating_factors: Reasonable apprehension of disruption of public peace from the accused's mass following; threats to witnesses and investigators; bribery attempts during trial; conduct in jail not above reproach.
other_sentence_order: High Court order of 24 June 2021 set aside, so furlough is not granted; pending applications disposed of.
